correctness.rationale: Fourier diagonalization gives nonzero eigenvalues 13+2c, 33, 40+2c with multiplicities 2,2,1. The resistance half-distances follow by applying the inverse to the nonconstant modes. For the coherence identity, ground i using B_xy=G_xy−G_xi−G_iy+G_ii with G=L⁺. Grounding j subtracts ||B_:j||²/B_jj from the trace. Row sums of G vanish, so ||B_:j||²=2e_r+6d_r² and B_jj=2d_r; hence C_r is a constant minus e_r/d_r+3d_r. Direct subtraction gives d₂>d₁ and C₁>C₂ since u−w>0 and every other factor in the factored difference is positive. Independent replay of the crossing used grounded blocks: with D=22+c, C₂=1/(D+1)+(3D²−2D−c²−202)/[(D²−c²)(D−1)−202D−40c], whereas C₃=4/33+1/(13+2c)+1/(31+2c). Exact integer-polynomial cross multiplication reproduces −P(c)/[33(c+20)(c+23)(2c+13)(2c+31)] for C₂−C₃. The resistance comparison has numerator 2c²+20c−103 and positive denominator. P increases on the positive axis, P(4)=−19521 and P(5)=58693, and 3<c_R<4. Thus both crossings and their ties are as claimed. Independent substitution verified the c=4 fractions; subtracting gives the stated exact gaps.
residual_risks: The classification is for the specified weighted graph family and pinned two-leader objective; the supplied symbolic checker was not executed.

value.rationale: In this two-leader model the exact positive-weight thresholds distinguish when a readily computed resistance proxy is valid from when it selects a strictly worse pinned pair. The complete ordering, ties, and small exact integer witness make the graph useful as a test case even with every edge present, a regime not classified by the related missing-edge family. Value rests on the exact separation and calibration, not on claiming the general phenomenon for the first time.
residual_risks: The exact phase diagram does not establish a rule for arbitrary circulants or leader-set sizes.
